en.title: Where to live in Cyprus: Limassol, Paphos, Larnaca and Nicosia
en.lede: The four cities differ in pace, in rent and in what is around the corner. The right one is the one that matches the week you will actually have.
en.desc: Limassol, Paphos, Larnaca and Nicosia compared on pace, rents, schools, hospitals and who each city suits.
en.alt: The seafront and buildings of Limassol

faq.a: Larnaca and Nicosia generally ask less than Limassol for a comparable flat. Paphos sits between them. A seafront unit in any coastal city leaves the middle of the range.
The widest choice is in Limassol, then Nicosia. Larnaca and Paphos have fewer places, and the known schools fill. Get an offer before you assume the flat comes with a desk.
In Paphos, yes, for most households. In central Nicosia, less so. A rent saving that ignores a car is not a saving.

faq.q: Is the coast always the better choice?
faq.a: No. Nicosia has the ministries, the main state hospital and a real weekday city. It is the wrong choice only if your week is the beach.

faq.q: Does the city change my residence permit?
faq.a: No. The permit follows the passport and the purpose. The city changes the rent, the school and the drive.

en.body:
Limassol, Paphos, Larnaca and Nicosia are the four places where almost everyone who moves to the Republic ends up comparing a lease. Famagusta district has towns on the government-controlled side, and the Troodos villages are a different life again. This page stays with the four cities. It is a comparison of pace, housing, and who tends to be comfortable there. It is not a ranking, and the asking rents are ranges for 2026, not an index.

## How the four cities differ

| City | Pace | Housing, asking rent for a one-bedroom | What is close | Who often fits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Limassol | Fast, coastal, the business centre | About €1,200–€2,200 | Port, marina, a long seafront, private clinics, many English-language schools | People who will work in the city and can pay for it |
| Paphos | Quieter, spread out, a large expat population | About €800–€1,400 | Airport, harbour, villages within half an hour | People who want a slower week and accept a car |
| Larnaca | Smaller, practical, the main airport | About €700–€1,200 | Airport, salt lake, a walkable seafront, improving new-build stock | People who fly often, or who want the coast without Limassol prices |
| Nicosia | The capital, inland, a real weekday city | About €700–€1,300 | Ministries, hospitals, the university, the divided old town | People who will deal with offices, or who want city life without a resort |

The rent bands are unpacked in [renting an apartment](/en/renting-apartment-cyprus/). A purchase, including the title questions that do not change with the city, is in [buying property](/en/buying-property-cyprus/).

{{figure:paphos-harbour-2024}}

### How to read the rent column

The one-bedroom band is a long-term asking range for 2026, not a week on a booking site and not a seafront penthouse.

## Limassol

Limassol is where the largest share of new international business has landed, and the housing market shows it. The seafront and the newer towers are priced for that demand. A flat a few kilometres inland, or in a western suburb, can be a different bill. Traffic at the end of the working day is the complaint residents repeat. The compensation is choice: restaurants, private hospitals, and more English-language school places than the other coastal cities, though the popular schools still run waiting lists.

It suits someone who will actually use the city: an office, a school run, a port client. It is an expensive place to keep a holiday pattern of sleeping and going to the beach. The beach is there. The rent assumes you are doing more than that.

### Who should not choose it

Someone who needs a ministry, a specialist clinic every week, or a particular English-language school with no waiting list should look at the other three cities first.

## Paphos

Paphos district is lower-rise and more spread out. The town, the harbour and the villages of the district attract people who have already retired or who work remotely and do not need to be in Limassol. English is widely spoken in the parts of town where that population lives. Public transport is thinner, so a car is the default. That cost belongs in the [driving guide](/en/driving-license-car-cyprus/) and in the monthly budget of the [cost of living guide](/en/cost-of-living-cyprus/).

Housing is cheaper than Limassol at the middle of the market and still not cheap in the newest gated projects. A village house looks like a bargain until you price the drive to a hospital, a secondary school and a supermarket that stays open late. For a family, check the school before you fall for the view. International and private options exist. They are fewer, and a place is not guaranteed. See [schools](/en/schools-kindergartens-cyprus/).

## Larnaca

Larnaca is the airport city, which matters more than the slogan suggests. A morning flight does not require a dawn drive across the island. The seafront at Finikoudes is walkable, the salt lake is a real piece of the town rather than a brochure, and the new-build market has grown without matching Limassol’s top prices. The town is smaller. Some of the specialist medical care and some of the school choice still sits in Nicosia or Limassol.

It suits a person who travels, a couple who want the sea and a lower rent, and anyone whose residence file or job does not require a daily presence in the capital. It is a weaker fit if your week is a series of ministry appointments.

## Nicosia

Nicosia is inland, hotter in summer, colder on winter nights, and the only one of the four that feels like a capital on a Tuesday. The ministries, the courts, the large state hospital and the university are here. Rents have risen, and they are still generally below Limassol for a comparable flat. The old town inside the walls and the suburbs outside them are different neighbourhoods. Engomi, Strovolos and Aglandjia come up constantly in family searches because of schools and services.

The city is divided. The crossing points are a fact of the map, not a reason to be casual about where a property sits. Buy and rent on the government-controlled side unless you have advice that deals, specifically, with the other. A title issued in the Republic is the title this site’s buying guide is about.

Nicosia suits people who will use the offices, students, and families who care more about a hospital and a school than about a sea view. It is a poor fit for someone whose plan is to live on the beach and drive to the capital twice a year.

## Infrastructure that actually changes the choice

Healthcare is national, through GeSY, once you are enrolled, and the large hospitals are unevenly spread. Nicosia has the main state hospital. Limassol has substantial private capacity. Paphos and Larnaca have hospitals and rely on transfers for some specialist work. Enrolment is explained in [GeSY](/en/gesy-healthcare-cyprus/). Do not choose a village on the strength of a clinic that is open two mornings a week if someone in the household has a condition that needs regular specialist care.

Schools follow the same pattern. Public schools teach in Greek and are free. English-language private and international schools cluster in Limassol and Nicosia, with options in the other two cities that fill up. Visit before you sign a lease that assumes a place.

The road network is good between the four cities and poor as a reason to live without a car in Paphos. Buses exist, and they are not how most residents do a weekly shop. Electricity bills, which are higher in a badly insulated coastal flat that runs air-conditioning all summer, can erase a rent saving. Price the bill, not just the lease.

## A short way to decide

Write down the thing you will do three times a week. An office, a school gate, a clinic, a flight. Put the home within a drive you will still accept in August. Then look at the rent range, not at the photograph. The [relocation guide](/en/relocating-to-cyprus/) is the residence and tax frame around that choice. The investment route, if the home is also the qualifying asset, is in [permanent residence](/en/cyprus-permanent-residency-300k/).

## Useful services

- A local agent who will show ordinary stock, not only the project that pays the highest commission. Ask to see the title or the landlord’s authority.
- A car, hired while you look and bought only once you know the district. Hire is the [car guide](/en/renting-a-car-in-cyprus/).
- Medical cover for the gap before GeSY, in the [health insurance guide](/en/international-health-insurance/).
- A tax sketch, if the city choice is really a residence choice, on [MyCyTax](https://mycytax.com).

## Property search and a document check

If you are deciding between two cities, or you have a lease or a contract and want it read before you pay, use the [property consultation](/en/property-consultation/). Say whether you want to rent or buy, and name the areas. The form asks for a name and an email. It is not a valuation. You can also write to [cynews24@gmail.com](mailto:cynews24@gmail.com).
